taxonomic_note: POWO accepts Bidens frondosa L. Source pool iNaturalist taxon 51712. Do not confuse with compound-leaved B. vulgata.
look_here_first: Find a middle stem leaf and count leaflets: B. frondosa is usually 3(–5)-foliolate, not simple. Then inspect the head: rays are absent or very short/few. Confirm with outer calyculus bractlets and mature barbed cypselae; avoid ID by head color.

project_inclusion.learner_admission_basis: Calvin-approved Master Plant Pool row 134 (My iNaturalist Flora); taxonomy and diagnostic review dated 2026-10-08
project_inclusion.range_basis: POWO supports Texas nativity at state level; three distinct target-zone county proofs not established. Source-pool membership is learner approval, not a native-range PASS.

morphology_keys.habit: Annual herb, often branching, frequently in moist or disturbed habitats.
morphology_keys.leaves: Leaves commonly opposite, usually divided into 3, sometimes 5 leaflets; leaflets toothed.
morphology_keys.heads: Small yellow disk heads; ray florets absent or few and short. Outer calyculus commonly 5–8(–10) bractlets (FNA).
morphology_keys.fruits: Flattened dark cypselae with retrorsely barbed awns; compare fully mature fruits and receptacular chaff.

comparisons.key_distinctions: B. laevis is perennial with sessile SIMPLE leaves and conspicuous yellow rays (usually 7–8). B. vulgata may also have compound leaves, so count calyculus bractlets and inspect fruit and leaf details rather than assuming all compound-leaved beggarticks are B. frondosa. B. cernua can share wet habitats but usually has simple leaves; confirm heads and cypselae.
